issues.description: Predicate is correct but reads obliquely; a small literate comment would make the invariant explicit.
issues.detail: The change hinges on a subtle CSS-spec fact: a bare `@layer foo;` statement is allowed before `@import`, but `@layer foo {}` with a block is not. The code expresses this as `!(nodeName === 'layer' && typeof node.nodes === 'undefined')`, which is correct but asks the reader to reconstruct the rule from a negation over a postcss internal. One line of comment stating the invariant would pay for itself.

issues.description: Prefer `node.nodes === undefined` (or an explicit helper) over `typeof === 'undefined'` for a structural property.
issues.detail: `node.nodes` is a documented postcss field that is either an array (Container) or absent (statement-form at-rule). A direct `=== undefined` check expresses the intent more plainly than `typeof`, which is idiomatic only for possibly-undeclared identifiers. Minor readability win; no behavioral change.

issues.description: Test coverage misses the symmetric accept-case: a layer statement (no block) before `@import` should still pass.
issues.detail: The new reject test covers `@layer foo {}` before `@import`. The literate-completeness counterpart — `@layer foo;` (no block) before `@import` as an accepted case — would pin down the distinction the predicate now encodes and guard against future regressions that flip the condition. Cheap to add and makes the invariant testable in both directions.

review.summary: RIGOROUS on the substantive change: the predicate correctly distinguishes the statement form of `@layer` (allowed before `@import` per the CSS Cascade spec) from the block form (not allowed), and the new test pins the previously-missed case. The fix is one token wide and asymptotically free — no complexity or data-structure concerns. The remaining notes are NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT class: the negation-over-`typeof node.nodes` reads obliquely, a one-line invariant comment would help the next reader, and a symmetric accept-test for `@layer foo;` would make the distinction testable in both directions. Safe to merge; the polish is P2.
